title: Silver Layer Contract v1.0.0
description:
Typed, defect-handled, versioned per-source tables. Each entry under `tables` describes ONE ROW of that table. Same dialect as contracts/lead_output.schema.json.

JSON Schema cannot express grain, referential expectations or a row-count floor, so each table also carries `x-table-constraints`:
  unique_keys   the grain, enforced on the _current slice
  foreign_keys  with optional orphans_allowed_when naming the boolean column that licenses a legitimately missing parent
  row_count_min a floor, so an empty build fails loudly

Column ORDER is part of this contract (x-column-order-is-contract). Silver must be byte-identical across rebuilds, and the writer emits the contract's order; a reordered contract has to fail loudly rather than silently rewriting every file with new bytes and identical content.

Enforced by src/contracts.py: types via DESCRIBE, everything else via generated SQL, all violations collected before raising. python -m src.transform.build validates every table BEFORE renaming any .part file into place -- a contract failure leaves the previous silver exactly as it was.

montgomery.crash.title: Montgomery County crash (Incidents, bhju-22kf)
montgomery.crash.description: One row per crash per version. Natural key report_number. SCD2 delta mode: deletions are NOT observable through keyset incremental ingest, so deleted_in_load_ts is always NULL here.

crash_datetime_local.description: Naive local wall clock exactly as published. NOT localised to UTC: that needs the coordinate-derived IANA zone and is Phase 4.

lat_raw.description: Raw source value, kept even when rejected. NOT range-checked -- that is the point: an out-of-envelope or sentinel coordinate survives here so the defect stays auditable.

lon_raw.description: Raw source value, kept even when rejected.

distance_from_envelope_m.description: Geodesic metres from the nearest edge of the configured envelope (WGS84 ellipsoid, pyproj.Geod). 0 inside.

number_of_lanes_raw.description: The unparsed string. 3,830 incident rows carry a comma-joined value like '2, 3' where the crash spans two roadway segments; number_of_lanes is NULL for those.

source_updated_at_utc.description: Socrata :updated_at as naive-UTC TIMESTAMP. 125,005 incident rows share 2024-06-12T20:28:27.326 from a bulk reload.

severity_ordinal.description: The single harmonised scale. 0 unknown, 1 no apparent injury (O), 2 possible (C), 3 suspected minor (B), 4 suspected serious (A), 5 fatal (K). See config/severity_crosswalk.csv.

severity_grain.description: Which rule produced severity_ordinal, so a max-over-parties is never mistaken for a source-published crash severity.

incident_string_matches_driver_rows.description: The crash-level substance concatenation recovered exactly driver_row_count parties. TRUE for 100% of NEW_PAIR crashes.

incident_string_matches_driver_distinct.description: It recovered exactly the count of DISTINCT driver values. TRUE for 100% of OLD_SINGLE crashes -- the old dictionary generation de-duplicates before joining.

substance_crosscheck_agrees.description: The Incidents concatenation and the Drivers rollup agree on both suspicion flags. NULL where the crash has no driver rows.

row_hash.description: md5 over the CONFORMED attribute columns only -- not over _bronze_* metadata, so a re-ingest under a new load_ts does not manufacture a version.

valid_from.description: Source mutation stamp where one exists (Montgomery :updated_at), else the bronze _bronze_load_ts that first carried this row hash. Never now(): silver is a pure function of bronze.

valid_to.description: The next version's valid_from. NULL on the current version.

is_current.description: Exactly one TRUE per natural_key, enforced by the unique key on the _current tables.

deleted_in_load_ts.description: The snapshot load_ts in which this key was first absent from its own scope. Always NULL for Montgomery -- deletions are not observable through keyset incremental ingest.

_bronze_load_ts.description: Lineage: the bronze partition this version was read from.

_bronze_row_sha256.description: Lineage: the bronze row hash (Montgomery/TxDOT) or the annual zip hash (FARS, whose unit of raw preservation is the zip, not a page).

_bronze_raw_path.description: Lineage: the raw payload file (Montgomery/TxDOT) or the zip member (FARS).

fars.codebook.title: FARS code dictionary, extracted from the data
fars.codebook.description: Every <COL>NAME label column, as (table, column, code, label, first_year, last_year). NHTSA's own labels out of NHTSA's own files -- evidence for the severity crosswalk rather than a transcription of the manual. Columns with more than 300 distinct codes are excluded: they label continuous fields, not code dictionaries.

silver.crash.title: Unified crash grain
silver.crash.description: One row per crash per SOURCE. A conformed grain, not an entity-resolved fact: a Texas fatality legitimately appears in both TXDOT_CRIS and NHTSA_FARS. Cross-source resolution is Phase 3, on top of this table.

crash_uid.description: Deterministic: source_system + ':' + source_record_id. Never random -- a UUID would break byte-identity on rebuild and make a lead id unstable across runs.

source_system.description: Matches the lead output contract's enum.
